answer.evidence: Most first-layer units (0, 4-7, 13-15, 19, 21, 22, 24, 25, 30, 31) look like near-initialisation noise: their weights rarely exceed about |81|, roughly the init bound for fan-in 576. The weights that clearly exceed that bound fall into broad or centred patterns. Unit 20 has a dense block of large positive weights over the central region, rows 9-17 and cols 5-12 (e.g. 88, 91, 86, 99, 92, 96, 90, 91). Its approximate linear contribution to the logit through layer 2 is positive, about +7.5k integer units (layer-2 weight x output weight), consistent with a bright, large central mass pushing toward malignant. Units 18 and 29 also concentrate large positive weights near the centre (unit 18: r15 c8-12 = 72 76 72 80 84; unit 29: rows 7-17, cols 7-16). Unit 18 projects strongly positive to the logit (about +30k by the same estimate). Units 1, 8, 26 and 27 are diffusely positive across the whole field, and units 3, 11, 12, 16 and 28 are diffusely negative; these act as global density/brightness detectors, not localized ones. Units 17 and 23 show weak top/bottom (17) and top/left (23) edge banding, with unit 17 negative in the centre, which reads as a periphery-vs-centre contrast feature. Their net effect on the output is small or slightly negative (about -0.7k and -3.4k). No unit has a compact, high-magnitude, same-sign patch at a corner or border that routes strongly to the output, which is the expected signature of an artifact or marker shortcut.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly responds to bright, dense tissue in the central region where the nodule sits (units 18, 20 and 29), plus global tissue density. Larger, brighter central nodules push the logit toward malignant.
